A further build above 65,000 contracts would take positioning into the zone where AUD reversals have historically originated; a decline would relieve the single clearest tactical headwind. The vendor legacy non-commercial series simultaneously reads −44.5k net short, and any convergence between the two series would clarify a genuine data ambiguity.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced — positioning data is published with a three-day lag and is a coincident rather than leading indicator.

key_catalysts.event: NAB Business Survey and Westpac–Melbourne Institute Consumer Sentiment
key_catalysts.rationale: The quarterly NAB survey showed business confidence at −19, thirteen points lower and twenty-two points below its long-run average, with conditions at +2 and below the long-run average for the first time since June 2025; the monthly series has confidence at a −6 prior and conditions at a +4 prior. Consumer sentiment rose 6.0% to 88.9 in August but remains deeply pessimistic. These are the RBA's named leading indicators for the demand side and the Board explicitly said it would watch the data flow before 28–29 September.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced. Australian survey data rarely moves spot directly but feeds the September hike probability.

key_catalysts.event: FOMC decision with Summary of Economic Projections
key_catalysts.rationale: Fed funds futures price a 60.4% probability of a 25bp hike following Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote, which stated that better summer inflation readings "do not tell me that underlying trends have meaningfully improved". The July meeting was a 9–3 hold with three regional presidents dissenting for a hike, so the committee is already leaning tighter. A hike plus a hawkish dot shift compresses the AU–US two-year spread from +49bp toward +25bp and places the dollar at the US-exceptionalism end of the smile, where AUD structurally underperforms.
key_catalysts.priced_in: The hike is 60.4% priced; the projection path is not. A hold would be the larger surprise and is sharply AUD-positive.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: AUD/USD is the direct expression; broad impact on all AUD crosses through the dollar

key_catalysts.rationale: The BoE held at 3.75% on a 6–3 vote in July with Greene, Pill and Mann dissenting for a hike, up from two dissenters previously, and all members agreed energy price risks are skewed to the upside. The AUD–GBP policy spread is only 60bp, the second-narrowest in the benchmark set, and GBP/AUD at 1.89003 sits at the 16th percentile of its annual range. A fourth hike dissent or an outright hike would compress an already thin spread.
key_catalysts.priced_in: A hold is largely priced; the vote split is the variable.

key_catalysts.event: Bank of Japan Monetary Policy Meeting
key_catalysts.rationale: The BoJ held at 1.00% on an 8–1 vote in July with board member Takata proposing 1.25%, and said core inflation is likely to accelerate "clearly above" 2% from the second half of FY2026. Consensus places the next hike at the 30 October Outlook meeting rather than September, so a September move would be a genuine surprise that compresses AUD/JPY carry from 335bp to 310bp with AUD/JPY at the 98th percentile of its range, within 0.26% of the 114.96483 annual high.
key_catalysts.priced_in: A hold is priced. A September hike is not, and would be sharply negative for the single most stretched carry cross in the complex.

key_catalysts.event: SNB quarterly assessment, Norges Bank Monetary Policy Report, Riksbank Monetary Policy Report
key_catalysts.rationale: Three decisions on one day covering the three widest and narrowest AUD carry spreads. The SNB has held zero for a full year with an increased stated willingness to intervene in FX, which sustains the 435bp AUD–CHF spread that underpins the most stretched cross in the complex at the 100th percentile. Norges Bank held at 4.25% in August saying a further increase is framed as one that "may still become necessary" rather than imminent (the stronger paraphrase previously used is flagged), leaving the AUD–NOK spread at 10bp. The Riksbank held for a seventh consecutive meeting while retaining hike probability for later this year, leaving AUD–SEK at 260bp.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Holds are priced across all three. The Norges Bank Monetary Policy Report rate path and the Riksbank's hike language are not.

key_catalysts.rationale: The single largest AUD binary in the tactical window. Roughly 47–50% is priced for a 25bp hike to 4.60%, up from approximately 17% before the July CPI. NAB expects the hike here; CBA, ANZ, Goldman Sachs and UBS expect November. The August minutes disclosed a live pre-emptive-hike debate and named monthly inflation, employment and housing reports as the deciding evidence, both of which have since come in hawkish. The statement language matters as much as the decision — removal of "including increasing the cash rate target further if upside risks materialise" would be a major dovish surprise.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Approximately half priced for the hike; the statement language is not priced.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: All AUD crosses; most acute in AUD/USD and AUD/NZD

key_catalysts.rationale: Australia publishes headline and RBA trimmed mean CPI quarterly rather than monthly, which compresses three months of expectations into one number and produces outsized AUD reactions. The Q2 print was 3.9% headline on the quarterly basis and 3.6% trimmed mean; the July monthly indicator was 3.5% headline and 3.6% trimmed mean. This release resolves the central disagreement in the market — whether the July acceleration was signal, as NAB, CBA, ANZ and Goldman argue, or "noisy rather than a genuine signal of reacceleration", as Westpac maintains.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced. It is the resolution event for the entire tactical thesis.

key_catalysts.event: Bank of Japan Monetary Policy Meeting with Outlook Report
key_catalysts.rationale: The consensus location of the BoJ's next 25bp hike to 1.25%, which compresses the AUD–JPY policy spread from 335bp to 310bp. Most policy board panelists expect one further hike by year-end and the BoJ has stated core inflation will run "clearly above" 2% from the second half of FY2026. AUD/JPY carry-to-60-day-realised-vol of 0.448 is the second-highest in the AUD complex and the cross sits at the 98th percentile of its range, so carry compression bites into a maximally extended position.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially — the hike is consensus but the accompanying Outlook Report inflation revisions are not.

key_catalysts.event: RBA decision with quarterly Statement on Monetary Policy
key_catalysts.rationale: CBA, ANZ, Goldman Sachs and UBS all locate the hike to 4.60% here. The accompanying Statement on Monetary Policy is the highest-signal RBA communication in the strategic window because it contains revised forecasts, and the RBA signals its rate path through forecast revisions rather than explicit guidance. The current SoMP has underlying inflation at 3.3% by end-2026, CPI at 3.6% in Q4 2027 and 2.6% in Q4 2028, with the 2–3% midpoint not reached until early 2028. An upward revision opens a path to 4.85%; a downward revision closes the cycle.
key_catalysts.priced_in: The hike is largely priced by November; the forecast revisions are not priced at all.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: All AUD crosses; this is the tactical-to-strategic handover event

key_catalysts.event: RBA decision and FOMC with Summary of Economic Projections
key_catalysts.rationale: An RBA hike to 4.60% by December is fully priced, so delivery is neutral and non-delivery is sharply negative — an asymmetric configuration. The FOMC the following day carries a priced path to approximately 3.90% by November and 4.20% by August 2027. If both deliver as priced, the AUD–USD policy spread compresses from +72.5bp toward +45–50bp by year-end, which is the mechanical core of our strategic Neutral.
key_catalysts.priced_in: The RBA hike is fully priced; the Fed path is partially priced with the December SEP unpriced.

key_catalysts.event: ECB (with projections), Bank of England, and Bank of Japan decisions
key_catalysts.rationale: A single 48-hour window in which the ECB publishes projections, the BoE MPC decides with three standing hike dissents, and the BoJ meets. Every one of these central banks currently holds a tightening bias: the ECB holds an open bias after its July pause, the BoE has three dissenters, and the BoJ is normalising. Simultaneous hawkish outcomes compress the AUD–EUR spread from 210bp, the AUD–GBP spread from 60bp and the AUD–JPY spread from 335bp in the same week, into year-end illiquidity.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Individually partially priced; the correlated outcome is not priced.

It is also the first meeting after the Q4 2026 CPI and sits at the outer edge of the strategic horizon, making it the point at which the market will judge whether the RBA is finished. Q1 commodity contract resets for iron ore and coal fall in the same window.

This would flip Factor 3 to Bearish at high confidence and amplify Factor 4 through a forced unwind of the 48,541-contract leveraged long.

invalidators.mechanism: because a 40bp further deterioration would take the labour market decisively past the RBA's own assessment that conditions have "eased by a little more than expected", force a reassessment of the full-employment side of the dual mandate, and remove the demand-pull component of the inflation thesis that currently justifies the tightening bias.

seasonality.pattern: Three documented AUD patterns are in scope. (1) The August-September Australian corporate reporting and 30 June financial-year-end hedging tail, which typically peaks in August and fades through September. (2) Q4 year-end portfolio rebalancing and USD funding demand in November-December, which historically pressures high-beta currencies including AUD. (3) Continuous Australian superannuation equity-hedge rebalancing across a roughly A$4.3trn system, which generates AUD buying as global equities rise and AUD selling as they fall - a pro-cyclical amplifier rather than an independent seasonal. Q1 commodity contract resets for iron ore and coal fall in January-February 2027, just beyond the six-month window but relevant to the terminal view.
seasonality.relevance_window: The August-September hedging tail is inside the tactical 2-4 week window and is now decaying. The Q4 year-end funding squeeze falls inside the strategic 1-6 month window (November-December 2026). Superannuation hedge rebalancing is continuous and relevant at both horizons.
seasonality.historical_magnitude: The reporting-season hedging tail is marginal, worth perhaps 20-40 pips of drift. The Q4 funding effect is larger and is amplified this year because reverse repo balances have drained to roughly US$100bn from a 2023 peak above US$2.5trn, leaving very little money-market slack; combined with the December central bank fortnight (FOMC 2026-12-09, RBA 2026-12-08, ECB and BoE 2026-12-17, BoJ 2026-12-18) this makes November-December the seasonally and structurally weakest part of the strategic horizon.
seasonality.current_alignment: The August hedging tail has been AUD-supportive through the month just ended and is now fading, which argues mildly against the tactical Bullish stance. Superannuation hedge rebalancing is currently AUD-supportive with VIX at 14.51 and high yield OAS at 2.63%, but reverses violently in equity drawdowns. The Q4 funding seasonal aligns with and reinforces the strategic Neutral. No other seasonal pattern is asserted; in particular no January effect or undocumented Australian pattern is claimed.
